root_idea.summary: The root denotes disturbance and movement in a thing: shaking, quivering, or being set into motion.
root_idea.development: From physical agitation, the lexicon develops related uses for self-movement, brisk animation, growth stirred by freshness, sound, commotion, and trials that throw people into turmoil.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form هَزَّ.
Displayed under the normalized Form VIII perfect citation form اِهْتَزَّ.

senses.definition: To shake strongly; to set something in motion.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic occurrence, the verb is the feminine singular imperative and is construed with بِجِذْعِ; the trunk is to be shaken or set in motion toward the addressee.

senses.definition: To become moved, stirred, or quivering.
senses.usage_conditions: An intransitive or quasi-passive use describing an object or living thing that enters a state of motion or agitation.

senses.definition: To become stirred with fresh growth and rise into vegetation.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of earth or vegetation after rain, where movement is associated with renewed freshness and the emergence or increase of plant growth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To walk with an elegant, proud, self-satisfied gait; to behave with self-conscious pride.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions involving shaking the shoulders or sides as a manner of walking or bearing oneself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To impart brisk movement or eager animation: to make camels or people lively and prompt, cause a pace or journey to bring someone quickly onward, or make someone cheerful and ready to act.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of causing movement, including urging animals by song and stimulating a person toward generosity or good action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause a plant or herbage to grow tall.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of winds or rains as the cause of the vegetation’s upward growth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The property of vibrating or quivering when shaken.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression for a spear that vibrates when it is shaken.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To quiver in flowing motion, or to dart or shoot with a quivering motion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of water in its running and of a star in its descent or shooting.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To move quickly or make a commotion and clamour.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a procession, cavalcade, or other moving train.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become brisk, cheerful, eager, or actively responsive to a matter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of camels urged by singing, a person ready to do good, a heart moved by joyful affection, or—figuratively—those who rejoice at an honored person’s death.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To subdue or render submissive; to become subdued or submissive.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The active and quasi-passive forms express corresponding sides of the same subduing relation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman’s brisk eagerness and rejoicing to do evil or mischief.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical entry explicitly applies this noun to a woman; the definition does not generalize that application beyond the stated usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Briskness, sprightliness, alacrity, or cheerful readiness, especially a disposition toward liberality, kindness, and beneficence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used of the briskness of camels when urged on by their driver.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A quick camel pace or manner of going, or the commotion of a procession or cavalcade.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may describe the movement of a train as it travels quickly or is thrown into commotion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A repeated or murmuring sound or noise, including the sound of boiling, thunder, a mill, or wind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Of wind, the term can also describe the lightness and quickness of its blowing; it may include the confused sound associated with a moving procession.
A plural form reported as having no singular.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A star shooting or darting down, or quivering as it does so.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description of the star’s rapid, quivering descent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sword characterized by fine, vigorous, or graceful vibration.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive expression for the quality of the sword’s movement.
A descriptive nominal expression for water in visibly agitated movement.
A descriptive expression for a person characterized by lightness of movement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Seditions, discords, wars, or calamities that throw people into commotion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural term for upheavals in which people are agitated by conflict, trials, or other trying events.

cautions: The Form I Quran occurrence is an inflected feminine singular imperative; the public headword is normalized to the perfect citation form هَزَّ.
The Form VIII Quran occurrences support both general movement and the specialized stirring of rain-touched earth or vegetation into growth; these are kept as separate senses.
